clue.text: Extra jam, perhaps, is popular

parts.note: in cricket a wide is one of the extras, runs not scored off the bat
jam is one example of something you put on bread, a spread

explanation.surface: A breakfast remark: an extra helping of jam is always a crowd-pleaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra' is cricket: a wide (a ball bowled out of the batter's reach) gives the batting side an extra run. '... perhaps' marks jam as just one example of a spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular belief is one held by many people, one that is common across a broad area.

clue.text: Pan's People finally aware of bigotry

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese frying pan

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word People

explanation.surface: Pan's People were a 1970s TV dance troupe, pictured here as finally waking up to prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan's People were the dancers on the BBC chart show Top of the Pops, so the capital P hides a frying pan.
explanation.definitionFit: The modern slang sense describes someone alert to social injustice such as racism or prejudice.

clue.text: Couple study advanced body parts

parts.note: a couple is a pair, a duo
a den is a private room for working, a study

explanation.surface: A pair of students making progress in their anatomy studies.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the first sections of the small intestine, plural of a Latin anatomical term, so organs of the gut.

clue.text: Lead from salt mine of Wieliczka possibly taken outside with excessive cleaning

indicators.note: the first group of pieces is placed around the outside of the word meaning with
the lead of a word is its opening letter, here taken from salt

parts.note: a pit is a mine, as in a coal pit
Wieliczka is a famous salt mine in Poland, so something from there is Polish; possibly marks it as one example
with means and, joining things together

explanation.surface: A guide to a Polish salt mine, with lumps of salt carried out and scrubbed far too thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken outside' means the joined pieces wrap round the word for 'with', which sits in the middle of the phrase. Wieliczka is a historic salt mine near Kraków.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from military boot-shining and means fussy, meticulous smartening and cleaning, often more than needed.

clue.text: Container of chopped-up garb and assorted gubbins, primarily

indicators.note: chopped-up says the letters of garb are cut up and rearranged
primarily asks for the opening letters of the words assorted and gubbins

explanation.surface: A bag for scraps of cut-up clothing and odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gubbins' is British slang for miscellaneous bits and pieces. The surface nearly describes the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bag for keeping scraps of cloth, so a container, and by extension any jumbled collection.

clue.text: Cary, in reality, mostly gets Victor to replace book of records

indicators.note: to replace says the letter for Victor takes the place of the letter for book
mostly means all of the name except its final letter

parts.note: the actor Cary Grant was born Archibald Leach, so in reality Cary is Archibald
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor's real-life file: Cary and a man called Victor swapping places in a ledger.
explanation.walkthrough: Cary Grant's real first name was Archibald; 'mostly' drops the D, then 'to replace' puts V where the B was.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to or kept in an archive, a store of documents and records.

clue.text: Some recipes from the east of impressive proportions

indicators.note: in an across answer, reading from the east means right to left, backwards
some says only part of the word recipes is used

explanation.surface: Some exotic recipes, brought from the East, on a grand scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters from 'recipes', and 'from the east' reads it right to left: RECIPES backwards is SEPICER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on a heroic, grand scale is said to be on a huge scale, like a long heroic poem.

clue.text: Interrogate male about liberal pest, maybe

indicators.note: about says the first pieces go around the letter for liberal

parts.note: to probe is to question closely, interrogate

explanation.surface: A political interrogator quizzing a man about an irritating Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is a nuisance, something troublesome; maybe flags it as one example of a difficulty.

clue.text: Criminal is captured displaying classic comedy prop

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked, set in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A crook is caught on camera holding a slapstick prop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie of cream or custard thrown in someone's face is a staple of slapstick comedy films.

clue.text: Clever leader is accommodating, at the moment

indicators.note: accommodating means housing something inside, so the ruler holds the other piece

parts.note: a king is a ruler, a leader
at the moment means now

explanation.surface: A shrewd leader who is currently being accommodating.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shrewd or sharp shows awareness and cunning, as in a meaningful, understanding look.

clue.text: Collusion? California loudly shows disapproval

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
an audience that hoots jeers noisily

explanation.surface: Accusations of conspiracy prompt jeers from California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' belongs to the meaning of the noisy jeering, not a sound-alike signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'in' this means secret partnership or conspiracy with someone; the question mark allows for the idiom.

clue.text: Possibly the aim of bowls and snooker players: to win big

parts.note: in lawn bowls players try to get close to or strike the small target ball called the jack
the aim of snooker players is to pot balls into pockets

explanation.surface: A sports quiz question: what do bowls and snooker players want, if not to win big?
explanation.walkthrough: 'the aim of' does double duty for both games: bowls players aim at the jack, snooker players at a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from gambling machines and means to have a huge stroke of luck or success.

clue.text: Backtracking oil producer's at first an advocate of Home Rule

indicators.note: backtracking means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: rape, the crop grown for oilseed, is an oil producer; with the 's it gives rape's
first is written 1ST, with 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An oil producer retreats, having first championed self-government.
explanation.walkthrough: Oilseed rape is the yellow crop grown for its oil. '1st' with the digit as I gives IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wanting a region to break away and govern itself supports independence, the cause of Home Rule.

clue.text: Field exposed when fencing is removed

indicators.note: the fencing of a word is its border, so its outer letters are taken away

parts.note: a bleak spot is exposed to the wind and weather

explanation.surface: A meadow left exposed after its fences are taken down.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for 'exposed' is not printed: think of BLEAK, as in a bleak moor, and strip off its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a poetic and crossword-favourite word for a meadow or grassland.

clue.text: Young dog and cat perhaps present Sesame Street?

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
a cat is an example of a pet
to present is to show

explanation.surface: A puppy and a cat starring in a children's TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is just a link here: 'dog and cat' looks like one pair of pets, but 'Young dog' and 'cat perhaps' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running US children's programme features Muppets, so it is an example of entertainment with puppets.

clue.text: State: "You look a state"

indicators.note: to state is to say, so the following words are to be spoken

parts.note: to take a gander is to look, so you look is you gander

explanation.surface: Someone telling a friend bluntly that they look a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' at the start means 'say'; 'You gander' said in a non-rhotic British accent gives the country. 'a state' ends the clue as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The East African country is an independent nation, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Understood female in Germany

parts.note: in, as in staying in, means at home
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A woman who was understood while living in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to the bottom of something is to grasp it, like measuring the depth of deep water.

clue.text: Clock catalogue

definitions.meaning: to clock something is to notice it, take it in
a catalogue is an official list or record

explanation.surface: Two nouns side by side, a clock and a catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means notice or take mental note of; as a noun it is a formal list or record book.

clue.text: Body fluid and fly found in mug

parts.note: pus is a fluid produced by the body at an infection
to hover is to fly in one place

explanation.surface: An unpleasant discovery of bodily fluid and an insect in a drinking mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' is not a cup but British slang for a gullible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is a gullible person, someone easily fooled or defeated, an easy target.

clue.text: Surprise promising young actress with time up

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means a letter is moved higher, earlier in the word

parts.note: a starlet is a young actress tipped for fame

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming actress gets a shock when her time comes.
explanation.definitionFit: To surprise someone suddenly is to give them a jolt or shock, make them jump.

clue.text: Reportedly spirit-like spirit?

indicators.note: reportedly says the answer is heard like another word

parts.note: gin is a spirit, so like gin would be ginny

explanation.surface: A rumour about a ghostly being that resembles a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'spirit' is alcohol, the second a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a genie of Arabian folklore, a supernatural being; the question mark marks the drink pun.

clue.text: New team in France getting discontented Ronaldo for nothing? Anything but

parts.note: onze is French for eleven, a football or rugby team

indicators.note: discontented says the contents are removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A new French team signs a disgruntled Ronaldo for nothing, or anything but.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantity that is anything other than nothing has some value, which is the mathematical meaning.

clue.text: Order grade to be changed, getting C for German

indicators.note: to be changed says a letter of the word for grade is swapped
getting introduces the new letter that comes in
for here means in place of, marking the letter to go

parts.note: a degree is a grade or level

explanation.surface: An instruction that a grade should be altered, with a German student given a C.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict or official ruling issued by authority is an order.

clue.text: Leaves note with answer

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone departs, leaving a note with a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: dried tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is made from the dried foliage of the tea plant, so leaves stands for it.

clue.text: I smell following purge, awareness essentially shot

indicators.note: following says the word for smell comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: to purge is to get rid of, so rid

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the centre letter of awareness

parts.note: a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Someone smells after a clean-out, their awareness essentially shot to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' is not 'ruined' but the fabric sense, as in shot silk that changes colour in the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot silk is woven so its colour shimmers and changes with the angle of view.

clue.text: Cash short? Study. Cash missing upfront? Study

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: ready, or readies, is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A student tight for money is told to study, and to study again.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives two routes: 'Cash short' (READY less Y), and 'Cash missing upfront' (BREAD, slang for money, less its first letter B), each followed by 'Study'.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a subject at university is to read it, a British usage.

clue.text: It cuts the chat at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something that silences the chatter of sailors on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A small axe is a tool that chops wood, so a thing that cuts.

clue.text: Salesman allowed European to be charged

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A salesman lets a European customer be billed.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged as in loaded or filled up, like a charged glass, means full to the brim.

clue.text: Lapwing loses it, twisting to give cry

indicators.note: twisting means turning round, so the remaining letters are read backwards
loses means the following word is taken out

parts.note: the peewit is another name for the lapwing, after its call

explanation.surface: A lapwing, losing its way and spiralling, lets out a call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' turns PEEW (what is left of the bird's name) back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed tears is to sob, which is crying.

clue.text: Religious office in hot periods abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A church post left vacant during a heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the clerical calling, the office or ministry of a priest.
